title: Scrutiny of v_c regressors: form is lossy (rank), going is a blind spot
author: modelling
summary: Audit of effective-v_c terms. (1) FORM is the dominant signal but coupled through a CENSORED rank proxy (relative-finish): winning by a nose vs 10 lengths both give pos=1, discarding the margin = the …
text: scrutiny of v_c regressors: form is lossy (rank), going is a blind spot scrutiny form speed-figure going critical-power methodology v_c audit of effective-v_c terms. (1) form is the dominant signal but coupled through a censored rank proxy (relative-finish): winning by a nose vs 10 lengths both give pos=1, discarding the margin = the velocity info. mechanistic upgrade: a speed figure from lbw (lengths behind winner) + finishtime -> velocity deficit in m/s, coefficient ~1 (kinematic), normalised to a going/distance/class par. data available in results_rich. highest-value, cleanest. (2) going is a real v_c modifier (soft ground raises locomotion cost, differentially by horse) that the residual diagnosis cannot see -- it's a race-level constant that vanishes under within-race renormalisation. systematic blind spot of the whole loop; needs a calibration-by-going instrument, not the residual regression. (3) v_c estimator is a one-race min-velocity heuristic; principled version is the critical-power hyperbola d=v_c*t+w' across multi-distance runs. (4) jockey is reduced-form + selection-confounded; a clean coupling would route it through trip geometry/policy not raw v_c -- leave for now. rating is well-incorporated (resid ~0). meta: the residual instrument is blind to race-level physics (going/distance/class/track) by construction -- it will keep finding within-race mechanisms and miss condition mechanisms.

title: Full power-balance EOM underperforms kinematic by ~1.4 nats/race (win-prob)
author: modelling
summary: Tried the most-fundamental mass coupling: run the power-balance EOM (hkjc.model.eom) in production so declared mass enters every term via Newton's law, with one allometric constant b. Built dynamics.w…
text: full power-balance eom underperforms kinematic by ~1.4 nats/race (win-prob) eom mass allometric negative-result physics-migration steady-state tried the most-fundamental mass coupling: run the power-balance eom (hkjc.model.eom) in production so declared mass enters every term via newton's law, with one allometric constant b. built dynamics.win_probs + a sim='eom' path in fit.py (kinematic-calibrated gains form_gain=4, w_prime_gain=2). result on a 42-race slice: eom winner-logp -3.68 to -4.38 vs kinematic -2.30. removing drag (cda=0) recovers only ~0.7; lowering tau/noise doesn't help. the eom's dynamics (accel phase, w'-depletion fade, power smoothing) compress the ability spread the kinematic sim preserves. key insight: the (m/m_field)^(b-1) v_c factor is not an arbitrary tack-on -- it is the eom's exact steady-state solution (v_c=p_c/(k_loco*m*g), p_c=k*m^b). it captures the win-determining mass->v_c physics at kinematic accuracy; the full integrated eom only adds second-order transients that are currently mis-calibrated and hurt. making the full eom competitive needs a from-scratch recalibration (gains up, noise down, fade/drag retuned) starting 1.4 nats behind, uncertain it matches. recommendation: bake the steady-state allometric law (first-principles, ready now); treat the full dynamic-eom migration as a separate greenlit project.

title: Mass coupling PARKED -- real residual but low-leverage (b=1 isometric optimal)
author: modelling
summary: Calibrated the steady-state allometric law v_c*(m/m_field)^(b-1) on the quick backtest. b=1.0 (no mass effect) is optimal; b=1.5->47%, b=2->-9%, monotone worse. Fine check: b=1.05/1.10 also worse than…
text: mass coupling parked -- real residual but low-leverage (b=1 isometric optimal) mass allometric parsimony low-leverage negative-result calibrated the steady-state allometric law v_c*(m/m_field)^(b-1) on the quick backtest. b=1.0 (no mass effect) is optimal; b=1.5->47%, b=2->-9%, monotone worse. fine check: b=1.05/1.10 also worse than 1.0. so despite the confirmed-real bodywt residual (t=+8.8, survives rating+class), coupling mass to v_c does not improve goodness-of-fit -- it is low-leverage on the winner's prob, the same lesson as draw. physical reading: b~1 = isometric (aerobic power and carrying-cost both scale ~linearly with mass, cancelling) => no net v_c effect. per parsimony (physics-plausible + real-residual is not sufficient; it must move the needle), mass is left out. the high-leverage lever remains w' (+1.4pp). eom/allometric_b/dynamics.win_probs kept as inert recorded infrastructure (default b=1). next: speed-figure form (velocity vs rank).
